title: Grateful Dead Live at Oakland Auditorium Arena on 1982-12-27

ai_review.summary: Matrix mix with crystal‑clear sound captures a tight 1982 performance highlighted by a smoking Scarlet > Fire, soaring Bird Song and inspired Garcia solos.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its tight, focused playing throughout most of the set, with standout versions of Bertha, The Greatest Story Ever Told, Bird Song, Let It Grow and the classic Scarlet > Fire transition. Reviewers rave about the “Sick Bits” matrix mix – crystal‑clear vocals, excellent balance and a splashy keyboard‑guitar blend – making this recording one of the most listenable 1982 dates.

ai_rating.rationale: All six reviews are 4–5 stars and consistently highlight both superb musical performance and high‑quality mix, giving strong confidence in a top‑tier rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Great sounding show with a clean, balanced mix; crystal‑clear vocals, tight instrument separation and no reported dropouts or muffiness.

standout_songs: Scarlet Begonias > Fire on the Mountain (Scarlet/Fire)
poor_songs: Playing in the Band (fast version) – less engaging for some listeners
show_quality.setlist_flow: Standard 1982 setlist that builds smoothly; strong opener with Bertha, a tight first two‑thirds, and an inspiring second half featuring extended jams and a powerful finish.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note Garcia’s total commitment to every solo note, describing his tone as perfect and his improvisations full of energy and purpose.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir is highlighted for wailing on “Donna” (Bertha) and delivering powerful rhythm/lead work throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland receives praise for an intricate, "splashy" sound that meshes tightly with Bob’s guitar, adding a home‑y, heartfelt texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drums are described as engaging and tight, driving the set without any noted issues.
